video_title: Meet Range: The AI Trying to Replace Your Financial Advisor
gist: Range, an AI-native, SEC-registered wealth manager (~5,000 clients, >$1B AUM, ~$750K+ average starting account, median client age 41), is attacking the 1% AUM fee model with a ~$3K flat fee, 35 advisers acting as product managers, deterministic planning/tax/investment software driven by its AI agent 'Rye', and an in-house AI compliance agent. The founders also argue that frontier-model agents are hollowing out seat-based SaaS such as Salesforce, Notion and Figma.

insights.claim: Range, an AI-native registered wealth manager launched in 2023, has almost 5,000 clients and crossed $1 billion in actively managed assets in summer 2026, with the founders saying it is quickly approaching $1.5 billion.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: An AI-first adviser is winning real HNW deposits, not robo-sized accounts. Its AUM growth is a gauge of how quickly assets are leaving incumbent RIAs and wirehouses.
insights.quote: we did recently cross a billion dollars of actively managed funds this past summer

insights.claim: Range's average client starts with over $750,000 (close to $1 million) in deposits, and its median client is 41 years old, versus an industry where Americans typically first hire a wealth adviser at about 52-53.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: AI advisers are pulling in affluent clients about a decade before incumbents normally get them, which erodes the future client pipeline of traditional advisory firms.
insights.quote: the median age of Range client right now is 41 years old

insights.claim: Wealth-advisory relationships typically start at age 52-53 and last 22-24 years, so clients mostly leave only when they die. Range is betting that signing clients at around 41 can produce a 30-35 year customer lifetime value.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: Winning clients earlier drives lifetime value in wealth management. If next-generation investors pick AI-native firms first, incumbents will struggle to win them back later.
insights.quote: So they leave when they die. That's basically how it works.

insights.claim: Range runs about 35 advisers for almost 5,000 clients (~140 clients per adviser) and closely tracks clients-per-adviser as its core automation metric. Each adviser covers investment, estate, retirement and tax planning.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: Clients per adviser is the key operating KPI for comparing AI-leveraged advisory margins with traditional RIAs. Per the founders, competitors have started talking about this metric too.
insights.quote: we track that ratio maniacally because that's an automation metric

insights.claim: Range charges roughly a $3,000 flat fee for planning, investment management and retirement planning instead of 1% of AUM. It says this is about 90% cheaper than incumbents, while its gross margin is at least 2x that of the best player in the industry.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: Flat-fee AI advice combined with higher margins points to fee compression for AUM-based advisers such as LPL, Creative Planning, Mariner and Corient, and to a repricing of RIA aggregator economics.
insights.quote: our gross margin is at least 2x better than any the best player in the industry

insights.claim: At Range, clients belong to the firm rather than to individual advisers. This is unlike independent RIAs, where advisers own the book and take it with them when they leave.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: Firm-owned relationships remove adviser-departure risk, a structural weakness in RIA and wirehouse valuations, and make AI-native advisers' AUM more durable.
insights.quote: you're a Range client. You're not like a FAD client or a David client

insights.claim: Some Range clients with millions of dollars on the platform have never spoken to a human adviser. They interact only with the AI agent Rye.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: This is early evidence that HNW clients will accept advice with no human involved, which is the main assumption behind AI-driven fee compression in wealth management.
insights.quote: We have clients that have been with us have millions of dollars parked that have never talked to a human.

themes.theme: AI vs. human advisers & the 1% fee

insights.claim: Range's CEO says publicly that AI is already better than a human financial adviser. He argues that public trust, not capability, is the constraint, and that trust will take 5-20 years to catch up.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: If the trust curve is the only barrier, adoption could arrive in sudden waves, similar to the e-commerce payments adoption the host compares it to, rather than gradually.
insights.quote: AI is 100% better than your human adviser today, which I know a lot of people will disagree with

insights.claim: Range's founders argue that frontier AI models have commoditized financial planning. In their view, the real differentiation in wealth tech is now compliance: showing that the AI follows the same SEC/FINRA rules as a human adviser.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: Planning software and CFP-led planning as a standalone value proposition may lose pricing power. The moats shift to regulated distribution and compliance infrastructure.
insights.quote: you do not need financial planning anymore. The the models are amazing.

insights.claim: A 1% AUM fee on a $3 million portfolio costs $30,000 a year, often for two to four meetings a year. Range's CEO says the 22-year median adviser relationship makes this a large cumulative transfer to advisers.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: The fee math is the pitch that pulls affluent clients away from 1% advisers. It is a direct revenue threat to AUM-fee businesses.
insights.quote: that's the most expensive dinner you'll ever go to in your life

insights.claim: Range's founders say most traditional advisers now just park clients in the S&P 500 with auto-rebalancing rather than using tax-advantaged strategies, which leaves them exposed to cheaper automated alternatives.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: If adviser value comes down to beta plus rebalancing, fee-based advisory revenue is exposed to low-cost automation and tax-alpha products.
insights.quote: What they're doing nowadays is just parking you in the S&P 500.

insights.claim: Range targets complex households, typically in their 40s to early 50s earning $400K-$800K with multi-state taxes, private-school kids and aging parents, and generally does not take clients with more than $10 million. The plan is to go down market later, following an 'Uber Black first' strategy.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: Starting with complex, high-value clients before going down market (as Uber and Tesla did) suggests that AI advisers' reach into the mass-affluent segment will come later and could be large.
insights.quote: I call it the Uber Black audience.

themes.theme: Software + agents as the product stack

insights.claim: Range plans to launch direct indexing products at about one-tenth the usual cost. Its founders note that Schwab raised its direct indexing minimums to $10 million.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: Cheap direct indexing for $1-10M accounts would pressure incumbents' premium tax-alpha offerings and SMA pricing.
insights.quote: We saw Schwab increase their direct indexing minimums to $10 million.

insights.claim: Range's margins come from deterministic in-house software (financial planning models, Monte Carlo simulations, tax strategy and investment rebalancing engines) that its AI agent operates with permissions, not from the LLM alone.
insights.speaker: David (Range co-founder & chief AI architect)
insights.so_what: An AI wealth platform's defensibility depends on its proprietary deterministic tooling and permissions layer. That is the thing to diligence when judging whether an AI-advisor claim is real.
insights.quote: AI is doing some of it. They're actually running a lot of the software David and team have built over the last four or five years and no one talks about that.

insights.claim: Range is building agentic actions in iMessage. Clients would text its AI agent Rye to execute tasks such as a backdoor Roth conversion, funding a trust, finding a notary, opening accounts and making trades.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: Agent-executed back-office workflows threaten the paperwork layer of wealth management. The host joked that this is bad for DocuSign.
insights.quote: we're working on tools where you can literally text message Ry our AI agent and have it do a back to a Roth conversion

insights.claim: Range's chief AI architect argues that the underlying system matters less than the interface it exposes to an AI agent: with the right tools and permissions, frontier agents can operate arbitrary software much as a human would.
insights.speaker: David (Range co-founder & chief AI architect)
insights.so_what: Value shifts from application UIs to agent-accessible interfaces and permissions. Software vendors whose value is mainly their UI or customization layer are exposed.
insights.quote: the actual system itself matters less than the actual interface into the AI

themes.theme: AI compliance as the regulatory moat

insights.claim: Range built an AI compliance agent that monitors all AI-generated client content for fiduciary duty of care, loyalty and supervision. The founders say industry players have asked to buy it and Range refuses to sell.
insights.speaker: David (Range co-founder & chief AI architect); Fahad Hassan
insights.so_what: AI-based supervision at scale could become the gating capability for AI advice in regulated finance, and a possible standalone RegTech category.
insights.quote: you'd be surprised how often when people hear this that are from the industry they ask us to buy our compliance agent

insights.claim: According to Range, there are no specific SEC rules on AI financial advice yet. Range treats heavy regulation as an opportunity: its chief legal officer was formerly senior counsel at the SEC, and a former SEC chairman sits on its advisory board.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: Regulatory positioning, not model access, may decide which AI wealth platforms scale. Watch SEC rulemaking on AI advice as a catalyst.
insights.quote: There are no specific laws as far as we are we're aware of at the SEC

insights.claim: Range ran its AI agent internally with its CFPs for years before releasing the client-facing Rye about a year ago. The CFPs' feedback encoded nuances such as starting annuity time-value-of-money calculations at end-of-period rather than beginning-of-period.
insights.speaker: David (Range co-founder & chief AI architect)
insights.so_what: Human-in-the-loop domain tuning over years is a barrier that new AI-advice entrants cannot quickly copy.

insights.claim: Range's CEO calls Salesforce useless for his firm and says Range is building its way out of it, because AI now lets companies build and maintain a custom CRM in hours without coding. That undercuts paying roughly $100 per seat.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: Supports the bear case on seat-based SaaS. Customization-heavy enterprise software is most exposed to in-house AI-built alternatives.
insights.quote: Why would you buy Salesforce for a hundred bucks a seat per person? There's no reason to.

insights.claim: Host Dan Nathan noted that Salesforce rose 22% the day after its latest earnings, even though guidance was not that strong. He attributed the move to the stock putting a floor under the worst-case SaaS-disruption scenario, helped by Benioff appearing alongside Anthropic's Dario on CNBC.
insights.speaker: Dan Nathan (host)
insights.so_what: SaaS stocks are trading on AI-disruption narratives more than on fundamentals, so partnership signals with frontier labs can drive sharp relief rallies.
insights.quote: Salesforce went up 22% the next day and I it wasn't that the quarter the guidance was that good

insights.claim: Range's founders report that internal use of Notion is declining daily, that Claude Design has 'ripped out' Figma for them, and that they are cutting paid tools nobody has logged into for weeks.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: Startup seat churn toward frontier-lab products is an early signal of revenue risk for collaboration and design SaaS.
insights.quote: Claude designs ripped out Figma.

insights.claim: Altruist, Range's custodial partner since day one, was acquired by Vanguard for $5 billion in cash about two weeks before the interview. Range has also added Apex as a custody partner.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: Incumbents are paying up for RIA custody and tech rails that serve AI-native advisers. Custody and clearing platforms such as Apex are strategic assets in wealth tech.
insights.quote: one of our uh biggest partners got acquired by Vanguard for for five billion dollars in cash. Yeah, Altruist.

insights.claim: Range's CEO sees US wealth management as a non-winner-take-all market with room for Schwab, Vanguard, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and others. He expects the first wealth-tech firm to capture the next generation of investors to gain outsized share, and says Range aims to become the 'JP Morgan of the next hundred years'.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan (Range co-founder & CEO)
insights.so_what: Incumbents are unlikely to be displaced outright, but new asset gathering at younger ages may shift toward AI-native entrants.
insights.quote: I don't think this is a winner take all category.

insights.claim: Range's founders, who use Anthropic as their core model, found Meta's Muse agent strong enough to book a Delta flight and an Uber end-to-end from a secure payment vault and to retune an Instagram feed through app settings. They rate Muse ahead of the competing agent Instinct overall.
insights.speaker: Fahad Hassan; David (Range co-founders)
insights.so_what: Consumer agents that act across apps (bookings, payments, settings) are becoming real. Distribution-rich platforms like Meta could become transaction gatekeepers.
insights.quote: Muse I would say overall is a better AI agent right now.
